kerakoll/biocalce-intonaco.source: Coverage Biocalce Intonaco: approx. 13 kg/m2 per cm of thickness

It does not say which dilution the consumption range belongs to, so the figure is treated as product as supplied, which is the safe side for ordering. Also available in 10 kg and 5 kg drums and 1 kg bottles. The sheet prints a single range of 0.08 to 0.15 and no substrate table, so the calculator offers the range rather than splitting it into rows the manufacturer never published.

mapei/eco-prim-t-plus.source: CONSUMPTION: consumption varies from 30 to 150 g/m2, depending on the porosity of the substrate and on how it is applied
mapei/eco-prim-t-plus.caveat: A fivefold spread, so the substrate choice matters more here than on any other primer. The sheet applies it diluted up to 1:4 with water on cementitious substrates, up to 1:2 on anhydrite and gypsum, and undiluted or 1:1 on existing ceramic, natural stone, wood and old adhesive residues. Also available in 10 kg and 5 kg jerrycans. The sheet prints a single range of 0.03 to 0.15 and no substrate table, so the calculator offers the range rather than splitting it into rows the manufacturer never published.

The sheet prints a single range of 0.15 to 0.5 and no substrate table, so the calculator offers the range rather than splitting it into rows the manufacturer never published.

kerakoll/keradur.caveat: A fourfold spread tied directly to absorbency, so the substrate choice is the whole answer here. Ready to use. On highly absorbent substrates the sheet asks for several coats, waiting until the previous coat has dried. Also available in 5 kg cans.

kerakoll/primer-uni.caveat: Ready to use, and the sheet sets the dilution by substrate: as is on non absorbent substrates and as a surface insulator on compact gypsum or anhydrite, up to 1:2 with clean water on compact low absorption substrates, up to 1:3 on powdery gypsum or anhydrite followed by a second coat as is, and up to 1:4 where the job is to bind dust. Also available in 5 kg buckets. The sheet prints a single range of 0.1 to 0.2 and no substrate table, so the calculator offers the range rather than splitting it into rows the manufacturer never published.

kerakoll/kerarep.reason: The sheet quotes coverage as approx. 1.7 kg per litre of gap filled, with a maximum permitted crack width of 3 mm, not a rate per square metre. The quantity follows the measured length, width and depth of the cracks being sealed.

mapei/adesilex-pg2.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.65 to 1.75 kg/m2 per mm of thickness

mapei/adesilex-pg2-tg.source: CONSUMPTION: 1.71 kg/m2 per mm of thickness

mapei/adesilex-pg2-tg.caveat: The sheet prints general reprofiling over large areas up to 3 mm, which is the default here, and allows thicknesses up to 1 cm in a single layer on vertical structures.

mapei/mapewrap-31.reason: Consumption depends on the type of fabric and the sheet prints a separate g/m2 table for each MapeWrap fabric range, running from about 900 to 1000 g/m2 on the lightest unidirectional carbon fabrics upward. Pick the fabric on the sheet's table rather than from an average.

mapei/mapewrap-31-sp.reason: Coverage depends on the type of fabric, unidirectional, bi-directional or quadri-directional, and on the height. mapei/dynamon-mr-3000.reason: A concrete admixture, not an area product. The normal recommended dosage rate is 0.5 to 2.5 litres per 100 kg of total cementitious material, so the quantity follows the batching, not the square metres.

mapei/dynamon-sr-1200.reason: A concrete admixture, not an area product. Typical dosage rates range from 0.5 to 2.0 litres per 100 kg of total cementitious material, with the optimum set by site trials, so the quantity follows the batching, not the square metres.

mapei/dynamon-sr-2400.reason: A concrete admixture, not an area product. For high performance concrete the sheet doses it at 0.8 to 2.0 litres per 100 kg of total cementitious content, with the optimum set by site trials, so the quantity follows the batching, not the square metres.

mapei/mapeair-foam.reason: A foaming agent for lightweight concrete, not an area product. The sheet works in volume of foam: one litre of admixture produces around 1000 litres of foam at a density of 50 plus or minus 5 kg/m3, and the dosage for a given job has to be set by site trials.

mapei/mapeair-la-p.reason: An air entraining admixture, not an area product. Average dosage is one 0.5 kg bag per cubic metre of mix, so the quantity follows the volume of concrete batched. Supplied in boxes of 30 water soluble 0.5 kg bags.

mapei/mapequick-af-70.reason: A set accelerating admixture, not an area product. Dosage in weight is from 3 to 10 kg per 100 kg of cement, so the quantity follows the batching, not the square metres.

mapei/mapetard-rcc-me.reason: A set retarding admixture, not an area product. The dosage in volume is generally between 1 and 6 litres for each cubic metre of mix to be batched, so the quantity follows the volume of concrete, not the square metres.
